text:
Minutes of the Companion Animal Travel Desk meeting at Aurelia Skyways.

Attendees: Leo Wilson, Arjun Nakamura, Cira Pell, Windmere, and Rosie.

We came on shift to sync across the skyport handoff workflow and the in-cabin routines. The ground team reported carriers are being moved carefully between services, with extra attention to calm handling and secure latching so no pet gets startled during transfer. The senior coordinator reminded everyone that passenger concerns should be listened to closely, then routed fast to the right onboard support so we keep stress low from the first boarding step to deck arrival.

On routing, we aligned on how we label each deck so desk staff and ground handlers speak the same language under pressure. Brightwater is the vessel name where the deck is called Larkspur Shelf for pets traveling through transit. We also reinforced that deck access expectations are shared in the log before boarding starts, so the right lane stays clear for carrier movement and leash checks.

For onboard responsibilities, Windmere is the person who handles pets on board and is identified as Cira Pell. We reviewed the handoff moments when carriers transfer from ground custody into cabin storage areas, including quick confirmation of pet comfort, water access steps when needed, and a check that Rosie is settled before passengers get fully seated. Rosie stayed calm during the walkthrough, so we used that example to standardize a short, steady approach: slow carry in, gentle placement, then a pause to let the pet orient.

Travelers Leo Wilson and Arjun Nakamura shared that boarding flow affects their comfort the most. We agreed to keep desk notes short but specific, especially when a passenger is anxious, and to confirm any special movement instructions with the onboard handler right away. The team also tightened the escalation path: if a pet shows stress signals, the coordinator logs the issue immediately and alerts onboard support without waiting for the next routine checkpoint.

Meeting ended.
